title: Declare and clear shared memory
prompt: Write shared_lines(ty, name, n). It returns the three lines that open a kernel's shared memory: the __shared__ array of n elements of C type ty, the loop in which each thread clears its share, and the barrier. shared_lines('int32_t', 'a7', 4) gives exactly the three lines above.
starter:
def shared_lines(ty: str, name: str, n: int) -> list[str]:
    return []

tests.expect: __shared__ int32_t a7[4]; | for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < 4; z_ += blockDim.x) a7[z_] = 0; | __syncthreads();
__shared__ float a5[4]; | for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < 4; z_ += blockDim.x) a5[z_] = 0; | __syncthreads();
__shared__ float a12[1024]; | for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < 1024; z_ += blockDim.x) a12[z_] = 0; | __syncthreads();
__shared__ int32_t a3[1]; | for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < 1; z_ += blockDim.x) a3[z_] = 0; | __syncthreads();
__shared__ float a40[256]; | for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < 256; z_ += blockDim.x) a40[z_] = 0; | __syncthreads();

hints: Return three strings: the declaration, the clearing loop, the barrier. Copy the punctuation from the listing above.
The loop's counter is always z_. It starts at threadIdx.x, stops below the array's size and steps by blockDim.x.
The middle line is f"for (int32_t z_ = threadIdx.x; z_ < {n}; z_ += blockDim.x) {name}[z_] = 0;".
explain: Three lines, in this order. The first declares the array as __shared__, so the block's threads all see the same one. The second is run by every thread: each starts at its own number and steps by the block size, so the threads split the clearing between them and no two clear the same element. The third is a barrier, so no thread reads the array before every element is zero.
